come_follow_me.title: “I Will Turn Their Mourning into Joy”
come_follow_me.summary: The Lord promised captive Israel a new and everlasting covenant, with His law written in their hearts, and said, “I will turn their mourning into joy.” Jeremiah's prophecies were written down by Baruch, Ebed-melech bravely rescued Jeremiah from the dungeon, and Lamentations reminds us the Lord's compassions “are new every morning.”
questions: What does it mean to have God's law written in your heart? (Jeremiah 31:33)
How was Ebed-melech brave, and how can we stand up for what is right? (Jeremiah 38:7–13)
How can Jesus Christ turn sadness into joy? (Jeremiah 31:13; Lamentations 3:22–26)

previous.title: “Before I Formed Thee in the Belly I Knew Thee”

daily.quote: I have loved thee with an everlasting love
daily.thought: Some things wear out fast, but God's love lasts forever. When have you felt His love?

daily.quote: I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them
daily.thought: Jesus can turn sad days into happy ones. Who can we comfort today?

daily.quote: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
daily.thought: Covenants are promises written on our hearts. What promise did you make at baptism?

daily.quote: Take thee a roll of a book, and write therein all the words that I have spoken unto thee
daily.thought: The Lord had Jeremiah's words written down so we could read them. What verse is special to you?

daily.thought: Ebed-melech bravely rescued the prophet. How can you stand up for what is right this week?

daily.thought: Every morning is a fresh start with the Lord. What can we do better today?

deep_dive._comment: Tap-to-open study popup (live landscape). Filled on the Saturday refresh from the official lesson page for week_of. Quotes must be copied verbatim (KJV / manual). See README 'Study popups'.
deep_dive.intro: When the Lord called Jeremiah, his job was not only “to root out, and to pull down” but also “to build, and to plant” (Jeremiah 1:10). Even after Jerusalem fell, the Lord promised a Messiah, “the Branch of righteousness” (Jeremiah 33:15), and a new covenant. When we make mistakes or feel sad, He promises: “I will turn their mourning into joy” (Jeremiah 31:13).

scripture_blocks.about: Comfort and hope for Israel in captivity
Jeremiah and Baruch write the Lord’s words; the king burns the scroll
King Zedekiah, Ebed-melech, and the fall of Jerusalem
Poems of sorrow, and hope in the Lord’s mercy

principles.title: The Lord will bring His covenant people out of captivity.
principles.explain: Israel would cry with “lamentation, and bitter weeping” (Jeremiah 31:15), but the Lord promised to gather them home again. He keeps His promises to us, too.

principles.title: “They shall be my people, and I will be their God.”
principles.explain: A covenant is a two-way promise with God. The new covenant isn’t just about looking good on the outside—God wants His law written in our hearts, so we choose right because we love Him.

principles.title: The scriptures have power to turn me away from evil.
principles.explain: Baruch wrote Jeremiah’s words on a scroll. King Jehoiakim cut it up and burned it, but the Lord had it written again. God’s word is worth protecting and reading.

principles.title: I can be bold in standing up for what is right.
principles.explain: Jeremiah was thrown into a muddy dungeon. Ebed-melech went to the king, then pulled Jeremiah out with ropes and old rags. The Lord promised to protect him because he trusted God.

principles.title: The Lord can relieve the sorrow I experience because of sin.
principles.explain: Lamentations are sad poems written after Jerusalem and its temple were destroyed. Even there, we find hope: Jesus Christ’s mercy is fresh every morning, and we can always repent.

key_verses.text: Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.
For I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.
There is nothing too hard for thee.
It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

quote.text: My plea to all who have fallen into this trap of the adversary is to never give up! Regardless of how desperate things may seem or how desperate they may yet become, please believe me, you can always have hope. Always.
quote.by: President M. Russell Ballard, “The Joy of Hope Fulfilled,” Ensign, Nov. 1992

questions: What does it mean to have God’s law written in your heart? (Jeremiah 31:33)
What promises have you made to God at baptism? How is He keeping His promises to you? (Mosiah 18:10, 13)
How did different people treat Jeremiah’s scroll? How do you feel about the scriptures? (Jeremiah 36)
What impresses you about Ebed-melech? How could you follow his example this week? (Jeremiah 38:7–13)
What in Lamentations 3:22–26 helps us understand the forgiveness Jesus Christ offers?

activity.title: Write it on your heart
activity.steps: Each person draws a big heart on a piece of paper. Read Jeremiah 31:31–34 together, then write inside your heart the things you learn about making covenants with God (and one promise you made at baptism). Bonus: find something that lasts a long time (like a coin) and something that doesn’t (like a banana) and talk about what “everlasting love” means (Jeremiah 31:3).

strength_of_youth.label: October chapter
strength_of_youth.quote: Ask yourself, “Am I honoring my body as a sacred gift from God?”

daily_by_weekday.Sun: Sabbath rest: recharge body and spirit; no screens at dinner.
daily_by_weekday.Mon: Phone out of the bedroom tonight; aim for 8–10 hours of sleep.
daily_by_weekday.Tue: Fuel up with water and real food; skip energy drinks.
daily_by_weekday.Wed: No vaping or harmful substances—your body is a temple.
daily_by_weekday.Thu: Choose uplifting media; scroll past anything that drags you down.
daily_by_weekday.Fri: Respect others’ bodies: no body-shaming jokes or comments.
daily_by_weekday.Sat: Get moving outside, and ask Christ for strength with a hard habit.

deep_dive._comment: Tap-to-open study popup (live landscape). Monthly: refresh when strength_of_youth.month changes. Quotes verbatim from the guide. See README 'Study popups'.

scripture.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?

deep_dive.intro: Your body is an amazing gift from your Heavenly Father. Having a body gives you increased power to exercise your freedom to choose between right and wrong.

teachings.title: Your body is in the image of God
teachings.explain: The scriptures compare our bodies to a holy temple, a place where the Spirit can dwell. Your body isn’t perfect now, but your experiences help you prepare for a perfect, resurrected body someday.

teachings.title: Body and spirit are connected
teachings.explain: Your soul is your body and your spirit together, so physical health and spiritual health go hand in hand. The Word of Wisdom teaches how to care for your body and promises blessings.

teachings.title: Treat your body—and others’ bodies—with respect
teachings.explain: When choosing clothes, hairstyle, and looks, see yourself and others as God’s beloved children with a divine destiny, not just bodies.

teachings.title: Strengthen your body, don’t hurt it
teachings.explain: Enjoy the good things God has given. Alcohol, tobacco, coffee, tea, and harmful drugs are not for your body or spirit—and even medicine can hurt if it’s misused.

teachings.title: Keep sacred things sacred
teachings.explain: Avoid anything you watch, read, listen to, post, or text that is meant to stir up wrong feelings, including pornography. If a situation makes temptation stronger, avoid it.

quotes: Ask yourself, “Am I honoring my body as a sacred gift from God?”
Do things that will strengthen your body, not things that will hurt or damage it.
The Lord has promised great treasures of knowledge to those who keep the Word of Wisdom.
Turn to Jesus Christ and His gospel, and you will find that weaknesses can become strengths.
deep_dive.blessings: A healthy body, free from addiction, also increases your ability to receive personal revelation, think clearly, and serve the Lord.
questions: Am I honoring my body as a sacred gift from God?
What is one habit (sleep, food, screens, exercise) I could improve to take better care of my body?
How does keeping the Word of Wisdom help me feel the Spirit and think clearly?
When I’m tempted, what can I fill my life with to invite Heavenly Father’s and Jesus Christ’s power? (prayer, scriptures, service)
How can I show respect for other people’s bodies in what I say, joke about, or post?
